description: Source/genre groups kept as formal CC/public-research audio but excluded from fine-genre training when the dataset label is too noisy for the current classifier target.

rules.reason: FMA jazz rows showed 0% fine Top1 and 0% fine Top3 in source/genre audit; retain as jazz macro evidence until explicit jazz substyle labels are available.
FMA drum and bass rows showed 0% fine Top1 and weak macro routing; hold out from fine DnB while preserving electronic macro coverage.
MTG-Jamendo techno rows behaved as broad electronic/rock/reggae material rather than precise techno; hold out from fine techno until a stricter four-on-floor techno subset is curated.
Validation audit found these MTG-Jamendo techno tracks are already predicted as techno Top1 by the stable model. Restore only this stricter subset to fine training; keep the rest macro-only.

These FMA techno validation rows were high-confidence hard misses with macro mismatch in fine-label-quality-audit. Holding them out from fine calibration improved official Fine Top3 and Formal Fine Top3 without reducing target-genre Top1.

These selectively restored MTG-Jamendo techno validation rows remained high-confidence hard misses with macro mismatch. Re-holdout improved official Fine Top3 and Formal Fine Top3 while keeping the stricter MTG techno subset mostly fine.
MTG-Jamendo blues rows produced 0% fine Top1 and were a common false-positive source for dub/techno; keep macro evidence only.
FMA folk rows showed 0% fine Top1 and 0% fine Top3 with inconsistent macro routing; keep as world/acoustic macro evidence only.
FMA trap rows showed 0% fine Top1 and 0% fine Top3; retain as black_music macro evidence until explicit trap examples are curated.
MTG-Jamendo jazz rows produced weak fine exact matches and acted as broad acoustic evidence rather than reliable jazz substyle examples; keep for jazz macro routing only.
FMA blues rows created repeated cross-genre false positives around dub, folk, and rock; retain as black_music macro evidence until more explicit blues audio is curated.
FMA opera rows behaved as broad classical/vocal evidence and confused the ambient/drone boundary; hold out from fine opera while preserving classical macro evidence.
FMA rock rows showed low fine reliability and contributed to electronic/ambient false positives; keep as rock macro evidence while MTG-Jamendo carries fine rock examples.
Source holdout experiment on 2026-06-30 showed MTG-Jamendo rock fine rows lowered Formal Fine Top1 and Top3; keep as rock macro evidence until cleaner explicit rock examples are curated.
FMA house rows were a repeated false-positive source for techno; keep as electronic macro evidence while MTG-Jamendo carries fine house examples.
FMA soul rows acted as broad black_music evidence and introduced fine-level confusion with dub/funk/disco; hold out from fine soul until explicit soul labels are curated.
jaCappella ballad rows are useful vocal/pop macro evidence but are not reliable full-arrangement fine-genre examples for the current classifier.
jaCappella enka rows are a cappella/vocal-only and distort fine arrangement features; keep only for macro/acoustic routing until full-arrangement enka is available.
jaCappella reggae rows lack the rhythm-section traits needed for fine reggae/dub separation; retain as black_music vocal macro evidence only.
